answer_1.quote: We propose CSJ as a downstream task of text simplification and cross-lingual scientific summarization to generate a coherent cross-lingual popular science story.
answer_1.outputs: popular science stories in German from English scientific texts

answer_2.quote: We evaluate all models with three metrics: (1) ROUGE (Lin, 2004) -R1 and R2 compute the uniand bi-gram overlaps to assess the relevance, and RL computes the longest common subsequence between reference and system summaries to find the fluency. (2) BERT-score (BS) captures faraway dependencies using contextual embeddings to compute the relevance. (3) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease (FRE) computes text readability with the average sentence length and the average number of syllables.

answer_4.quote: We hired five annotators and provide them with 25 randomly selected outputs (of each model) from SSR and mBART with their original texts and gold references.
answer_4.guideline: The annotators were asked to evaluate each document for three linguistic properties on a Likert scale from 1 to 5. The judges were asked to rank the overall summary compared to the gold summary.
